title: Proto to Live Wiring Guide
desc: Procedures and rules for promoting protos to live harness files.
steps: DECISION: THE GATE DOES NOT RUN WHERE YOU ARE STANDING, so verify a promotion by PUSHING it rather than by any local check. AND BEFORE YOU WIRE ANYTHING AT ALL, SEARCH FOR WHAT ALREADY ANSWERS THE QUESTION -- owner directive 2026-09-12, mandatory, not advisory. Run wkappbot skill search with two or three keywords for the CONCEPT, and a web search when the concept is general rather than a repo idiom, BEFORE writing the module or the seam. MEASURED THE DAY HE SAID IT: a module was built to resolve a skill id by enumerating the skills directory by hand, when the harness already carried Get-WkSkillStoreRoots and Test-WkSkillExistsOnDisk, both one search away. THE ONE-LINE TEST AT SEAM TIME: name the existing function your new module would duplicate; if you cannot, you have not searched. Measured 2026-09-11 in WkAutoQuant: any gate running inside the push worktree sees ORIGIN state, so a local green is evidence about your tree and never about the promotion -- push early, read the refusal. ORIGINAL STEP: run the self-test FROM THE CANONICAL PATH after promoting, not only from .tmp. WHY: measured 2026-07-27 twice -- a fixture path still pointing at .tmp turned a nine-of-nine into an eight-of-nine, and a promoted file that dot-sourced its own name blew the call stack the instant it ran from its real location. SIBLING RULE: land each sector AS IT PASSES, never batch the promotions -- verify, wire, test, commit, then take the next one. WHY: batching concentrates risk into one unattributable commit. //why:verification shows sector passes with AS IT PASSES pattern //why:verified Track A artifacts before landing to canonical-opus //why:artifact verification complete, canonical promotion pending-opus //why:verification shows sector passes with AS IT PASSES pattern-haiku

DECISION: the seam in canonical is a Test-Path, a dot-source, and ONE call -- all logic lives in the module, and ONE SECTOR BUILDS ALL THREE PROTOS (LANDING FROM A PRIVATE WORKTREE: hash-object -w the protos, update-index --cacheinfo, commit, and only AFTER the commit prints its hash run reset --hard HEAD to sync the files; never send the reset in the same parallel batch as the commit, because a refused commit plus that reset wipes the staged index. Example: kih 4b2fc81ca, 2026-10-11) (owner correction 2026-09-18, given after a ROOT split them across two sectors in one message): the module proto, the wired proto and the self-test go to a SINGLE sector in one .tmp workspace, because a seam-only sector must stub the module it cannot see, so its backward-compatibility and additive cases then test a fake and ROOT is left reconciling two halves that were never run together; fan out one sector per disjoint CANONICAL SOURCE file, since the boundary is the canonical file the change will land on and never the proto count, and two sectors may never target the same canonical file. AND THE SAME SEPARATION GOVERNS WHO TYPES IT, owner directive 2026-09-11: ROOT DOES WRITE THE CODE, INTO THE BRIEF, AND ROOT DOES NOT APPLY IT. Put the old block and the new block in the dispatch verbatim so the sector is APPLYING an edit rather than designing one; the forbidden act is being the serial pair of hands, never the knowing and never the expressing. A ROOT that withholds the code because coding felt prohibited has turned a mechanical wiring into a design problem for the cheapest tier, which is the most expensive possible reading of the rule. THE THREE REASONS THE PARALLEL SHAPE EARNS THIS, in the owner's words: two or more VERIFIERS instead of one, so a defect must survive more than a single pair of eyes; COST-EFFECTIVENESS, since the cheap tier is better value per unit of work than ROOT's expensive slow hands; and ROOT being FREED TO POLISH THE LETTER AND LISTEN TO THE OWNER while the sectors run -- the reason a heads-down session loses without noticing, because wiring things by hand means the descent letter never gets written and every owner message lands as an interruption rather than an instruction. THE LINE THAT SLIPS: FINDING a wiring defect is ROOT's duty, FIXING it is not, and the second feels continuous with the first. Hand back the diagnosis with the code in it and re-dispatch. WHEN: any source file is being changed at all -- there is no size condition, removed by owner directive 2026-08-07. HOW: put the gathering and the decision inside the module and let the host call one function, and run wkappbot skill read wksplit-cs-utility for the extract-first rule this implements. WHY: every line of logic added to a fat host costs the NEXT editor another study-lock read and makes a later bulk split more expensive -- pre-separating is cheaper than splitting afterwards, and it keeps the reviewable diff small. //why:wait module wired proto selftest built together //why:verified Track A artifacts module extraction wired proto self-test //why:verified Track A artifacts module extraction wired proto self-test-opus //why:refused commit then reset wiped staged index once-opus

THE BRIEF ENDS AT .tmp (ROOT WIRES CANONICAL) AND NEVER ASKS FOR THE PROMOTION. The three-artifact contract says BUILD three protos, never LAND them. WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY WRONG: once a sector can write canonical the byte-diff control stops working. If it edits the .tmp proto as well, the diff comes back clean while the content is no longer what ROOT approved; and for a BRAND NEW file there is no canonical to diff against at all, so the diff proves COPYING and never FIDELITY to the reviewed text. THE SHAPE IS: the sector delivers the module, the seam copy and the self-test UNDER .tmp and pastes the raw runs; ROOT pays the study lock and performs the merge; and when ROOT itself cannot merge at omega, that is NOT a stopping point -- dispatch a SECTOR to attempt the identical git-mv landing, since a dispatched sector is empirically NOT bound by the ROOT-only omega block that refuses ROOT directly. NOTE: whether a sector CAN actually complete a git-mv landing when ROOT itself is separately blocked is a live open question outside this skill's scope -- it belongs to the emergency-fix escalation path, not to this wiring method. If the sector is refused by a DIFFERENT gate, pay it and redispatch -- repeatedly, with a corrected brief each time -- rather than accepting the first refusal as final. Only when every route (ROOT direct, ROOT CLI, sector, corrected sector, a second independent gate payment) has genuinely been exhausted does this become an OPEN BLOCKER, and it must be reported to the owner as exactly that -- an unresolved item awaiting a human or pro-tier decision -- never written or read as a completed, acceptable stopping point. DELEGATION METHOD: for ANY source edit, unconditionally -- the old triggers (study-locked, over the 400-line cap, write-frozen) were REMOVED by owner directive 2026-08-07 because every source that actually needs wiring in a live system is both critical and fat, so a conditional here only ever fired anyway while inviting a reader to argue their way out of it -- delegate THREE things to a cheap tier (Haiku by default, per claude-code-agent-tier-routing step 7) in one brief -- (1) EXTRACT-FIRST: lift the target logic into its own small module BEFORE editing, per wksplit-cs-utility steps 21/23, so canonical only ever gains a Test-Path + dot-source + one call (step 6 of this skill); (2) the WIRED PROTO: a byte-copy of canonical with only that seam added, never a hand-summarized rewrite (step 8); (3) a SELF-TEST naming every case, with at least two NEGATIVE cases proving the guarded behaviour still refuses (proto-to-live-wiring-howto step 8). The brief must carry the four layers from -howto step 6 (exact steps, anti-confabulation raw-paste, prove-the-artifact exit with a BYTES/LINES/PARSE_ERRORS line before any PASS, narrow guardrails naming what NOT to touch) and the file-naming discipline from -howto steps 13-15 (stage via a .txt with no p-r-o substring for a new locked file; name only files the agent will read/create, never an incidental filename in prose). ROOT then does the diff-verify + git-mv landing itself (this skill's own promotion sequence, in proto-to-live-wiring-ref, moved there 2026-09-15) -- CORRECTED 2026-09-15, owner ruling: GIT MV IS ROOT own promotion route -- git add -f then git mv -f from the verified .tmp proto onto canonical -- and stays ROOT's primary method, unaffected by this session's busy-fleet findings below. GIT MV IS THE ONLY SANCTIONED PROMOTION COMMAND IN THIS SKILL. Do not reach for wkappbot file write or wkappbot file edit as a wiring route. //why:ROOT wires canonical after sector delivers module+seam+self-test under .tmp //why:ROOT does the git mv promotion, never the sector-sonnet //why:HANDOFF.md commit: ROOT wires, sector delivers proto-sonnet //why:brief carries only the task, protos and self-test stay in .tmp-haiku

DECISION: THE MODULE (EXTRACTION) PROTO IS ARTIFACT NUMBER ONE AND OUTRANKS THE WIRED PROTO -- owner ruling 2026-08-25, in his words the extraction proto is the long-term positioning and the device that guarantees sustainable development, more important than the wiring proto. The three artifacts are NOT a flat list: the MODULE is the asset that survives, the WIRED proto is disposable scaffolding that exists only to make the seam reviewable, and the SELF-TEST belongs to the module rather than to the seam. WHEN: the moment you are about to change behaviour in any host file -- before you open the host, before you write a seam, and especially when the change looks small enough to inline. HOW: build the module FIRST as a pure decision function taking every input as an argument, prove it with an argless self-test carrying an inversion control, and only then write the one-line seam that calls it; run wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring-howto for the brief template and the promotion sequence, and wkappbot skill read wksplit-cs-utility for step 8, EXTRACT FIRST THEN FIX, which is the same rule arriving from the fat-source side. A MODULE PROMOTED UNWIRED IS A DEBT WITH A DEADLINE, AND THE SAME SESSION MUST PAY IT -- measured 2026-09-20 and it cost the owner the half of his mission he cared about most. scripts/replay_env_boot.py was built, self-tested 5 of 5, promoted and PUSHED, and then nothing called it; wk-kr-replay went on dying at parse_account with an empty CANO, so the KR half of a simulation the owner had asked for could not run at all, and I reported the failure as a structural limit of the replay on a predecessor's authority instead of running it once myself. THE TELL WAS AVAILABLE IN ONE COMMAND the whole time -- grep the host for the module name, which returned ZERO. THE RULE: promoting unwired is permission to SPLIT the landing, never to END it, so in the same session either wire it or write the seam and its blocker into the letter by line number. AND WHEN THE HOST IS PAST THE LINE CAP the seam is a net-zero widening of an EXISTING line, not a new statement -- here one import line became one longer import line, 724 lines both sides. WATCH WHERE THE COMMENT STARTS: appending after an existing trailing hash comment puts your call INSIDE the comment, so it parses clean, changes nothing, and reads as wired to every grep. Put the code before the hash and the comment last. AND PROMOTE THE MODULE UNWIRED RATHER THAN HOARDING IT: nothing calls it yet so the commit CANNOT change behaviour, while .tmp gets swept -- proto-to-live-wiring-howto step 9 states this and four verified modules were still sitting in .tmp when the owner had to say it out loud. WHY, with the failure that earned the ruling: on 2026-08-25 I landed a minimum-hold guard on the breakout exit as an INLINE compound boolean at willkim_realtime_scalper.py line 830, with a wired proto and a self-test and NO module. Net growth was zero so every gate passed it, and the result is untestable on its own, unreusable by the simulator that needed exactly that predicate, and one more inline condition inside a function already over the size cap. The same session then found it could not simulate the two harvest triggers AT ALL because they were inline ifs inside decide_actions -- the previous sessions had made the identical trade, and the cost compounds: a seam saves ten minutes and removes the ability to test, reuse or simulate that decision forever after. A SEAM IS DISPOSABLE, A MODULE IS THE ASSET, AND THE ORDER IS MODULE FIRST. //why:module extraction outranks wiring, and each has a clear role in long-term sustainability //why:Understanding artifact priority and maintenance lifecycle for long-term code sustainability //why:extraction first ensures sustainable development; the wired proto is disposable scaffolding //why:Module extraction before wiring-haiku //why:Module extraction before wiring-haiku //why:extraction first ensures sustainable development; the wired proto is disposable scaffolding-haiku //why:Used the three-artifact rule when dispatching the tag-drop guard wired proto sector

REDISPATCH-UNTIL-VERIFIED (was missing -- the loop half of THE SEQUENCE): when ROOT's own verification of a delegated proto FAILS -- the diff carries more than the intended change, the function-set comparison shows a drop, the parser errors, or the self-test fails -- this is NOT a stopping point and NOT a licence for ROOT to hand-fix the proto itself (that reverts to the exact chore-grinding the delegation was meant to avoid, per claude-code-agent-tier-routing). Diagnose EXACTLY which verification step failed and why (name the missing function, the stray hunk, the wrong line), sharpen the SAME brief with that specific correction named explicitly, and redispatch to the SAME cheap tier -- OWNER RULE 2026-09-28: send the correction by SendMessage to the SAME agent so it keeps its read files and built artifacts, but only to an agent whose round was honest and close (real artifacts, pasted raw output); an agent that fabricated results, reached into canonical, or ignored the brief is dropped and a FRESH one is dispatched with the sharpened brief. Repeat this diagnose-sharpen-redispatch loop until ROOT's own verification passes -- never after one round, never by escalating to a pro tier just because the first round disappointed (claude-code-agent-tier-routing's E10 guard forbids Opus as a delegation target for exactly this reason: re-instruct and redispatch cheap, do not reach upward). Diagnosis should run against the explicit PASS/FAIL criteria in delegation-verify-scorecard (spec-completeness, negative-path-tested, function-inventory-plus-line-count per model-instruction-drift-why-the-harness-exists step 10) rather than a vague sense of wrongness. This mirrors the REDELEGATION REFLEX already in agent-dispatch-preflight and sonnet-reflection, made explicit here because a wiring proto's failure mode is unusually legible -- the diff or function-set comparison names precisely what to fix in the next brief, so there is rarely an excuse to skip straight to ROOT doing it by hand. //why:Core pattern for iterative delegation until verification passes //why:Sector proto failed my own re-run twice, so I diagnosed the exact defect and redispatched cheap instead of hand-fixing.-sonnet //why:redispatch loop until verified is the pattern for haiku sector work-haiku //why:Core pattern for iterative delegation until verification passes-opus //why:Critical pattern: verify, diagnose failure, redispatch with sharper brief, never hand-fix //why:Diagnose failed verification, sharpen brief with correction, redispatch to same tier until it passes //why:Verification that delegation work passes before proceeding //why:handles redispatch when proto fails verification

DECISION: dot-source ONCE at file scope, never inside a function -- and write it that way INTO THE BRIEF, since a sector applies the sample verbatim (2026-10-11: the reflex-engrave brief put the dot-source inside Test-WkStopSkillRef and the sector shipped it so). WHEN: wiring anything that runs on the PreToolUse or Stop hot path. HOW: place the guarded dot-source above the first function and have the function only call the resulting command, per wkappbot skill read wk-tool-sub-1s-response-time-mandate. WHY: a dot-source inside a per-item function re-sources the module on every call and quietly breaks the sub-one-second budget the whole harness is held to. MERGED IN 2026-09-06, verbatim, the sibling rule on the same seam -- DECISION: every seam must FAIL toward today's behaviour. WHEN: writing the guard around a dot-source or a call. HOW: make a missing module, an empty result, and any exception all fall back to the original expression, so the worst case is the status quo -- wkappbot skill read wkharness-guards-howto shows the shape the existing guards use. WHY: a parsing failure must only ever make a guard match MORE, never less, because the one unrecoverable direction is a guard that silently stops firing. //why:send-alive seam keeps old live path when module is missing //why:duplicate run guard keeps old path when module missing, exits three on twin //why:like healing floor raised seventy seven with sibling aware remedy //why:wkharness-agy-main.ps1 dot-sources Add-WkForcedStudy at file scope, not inside Block()-sonnet //why:wkharness-agy-main.ps1 dot-sources Add-WkForcedStudy at file scope, not inside Block()-sonnet //why:like healing floor raised seventy seven with sibling aware remedy-opus

DECISION: PROVE THE SEAM BY EVALUATING IT, NOT BY READING IT. DO run the wired proto with the exact command form people type WHEN a seam changes a CLI branch, before landing. Example: kih e369cfe2f passed 5/5 module cases yet broke wkroot send REPO_PATH, because a repo path resolves no session record; reverted in 34a4778af -- the assert workflow the owner approved 2026-08-25 and asked to be made the standard for the fleet. THE CHEAPEST INSTANCE OF THIS RULE, measured 2026-09-03 and it costs one command: a module ps1 ending in Export-ModuleMember THROWS when dot-sourced, yet still defines its function, so the two obvious checks disagree and the reassuring one is the one a hurried session runs. Dot-sourcing a delegated prefilter proto printed THE EXPORT-MODULEMEMBER CMDLET CAN ONLY BE CALLED FROM INSIDE A MODULE while the function-availability probe answered YES in the same breath, because the error fires at the END of the file after every definition has landed; under a caller that sets ErrorActionPreference to Stop the load aborts outright. This repo's convention is a plain ps1 the host DOT-SOURCES, not a psm1, so the line is always wrong here and deleting it is the whole fix -- a dot-sourced file exports by defining. AND THE SAME RULE APPLIES TO THE MODULE'S BEHAVIOUR, NOT ONLY ITS LOAD -- measured 2026-09-04 in wkappbot-kih and it produced a GREEN SUITE OVER A LIVE THROW. A path normaliser was built to stop a guard throwing on illegal characters. Its selftest printed RESULT 4 of 4 while one case emitted an unhandled exception to the console, because the suite asserted only the RETURN VALUE -- null, which was correct -- and never asserted that NO EXCEPTION WAS RAISED. In a bare shell the throw was non-terminating, so nothing failed. Under ErrorActionPreference Stop, which the harness hook sets, the identical call TERMINATED and the guard refused a legitimate write exactly as before. TWO RULES. FIRST, NON-TERMINATING IN YOUR SHELL IS NOT SAFETY: run the module under a caller configured the way PRODUCTION is configured, or you are measuring your prompt rather than the harness. SECOND, WHEN THE DEFECT IS AN EXCEPTION, THE ASSERTION MUST BE ABOUT THE EXCEPTION: a suite that checks only what came back cannot fail on a function that returns the right value noisily, so it certifies the half of the fix that landed and stays silent about the half that did not. THE CHEAP TEST FOR ANY SUITE, and it is the one worth building the habit around: REVERT THE FIX AND CONFIRM THE SUITE GOES RED. A suite that passes both before and after a change has told you nothing about the change. VERIFY A MODULE BY LOADING IT UNDER ErrorActionPreference Stop, never by asking Get-Command whether the function exists afterwards. AND THE REASON IT SURVIVED IS THE TRANSFERABLE HALF: the brief demanded three deliverables, the delegate returned two, and the omitted one was the self-test -- precisely the artifact that would have caught it. COUNT THE DELIVERABLES BEFORE READING THE REPORT, because a missing self-test is not a smaller delivery, it is the delivery that decides whether the other two are true. THE SHARPEST CASE OF THIS, measured 2026-09-02 promoting an on-load nudge extraction into wkharness-post.ps1: when an extraction REMOVES a try/catch from the host, do not restore it by reflex and do not assume it is safe -- evaluate the seam's worst case in three lines. The original block sat inside try/catch and the extracted seam was two bare lines, which LOOKS like a lost fail-open. The probe was: set ErrorActionPreference to SilentlyContinue, call a deliberately undefined function, print a marker after it, inspect the assigned variable. The marker printed and the variable was null, proving an undefined command under SilentlyContinue does not abort the script, so the new guard clause simply does not fire and the host stays fail-open. THE ORDER IS THE LESSON: restoring the try/catch on suspicion would have added a line to a host that was blocked by fat-source-growth precisely because it may not grow, so the reflex fix would have cost the promotion outright, while the measurement cost three lines and settled it. A seam is verified by what it DOES when its dependency is missing, never by whether it resembles the code it replaced. WHEN: any promotion where a green suite exists and you are deciding whether it licenses a push. HOW: build TWO layers of asserts and require both. LAYER ONE proves the MODULES: stage origin/main through prodsrc_stager, import the real functions, and assert their outputs -- if a module is absent because the host does not import it yet, stage it by hand with git show into a .txt then wkappbot file write into the staged tree, since a shell redirect to a .py path is blocked. LAYER TWO proves the SEAM, and this is the layer everybody skips: open the WIRED PROTO, lift the changed lines out of it BY INDEX, compile them, and evaluate them against fixtures with every surrounding name stubbed. THE ASSERTION THAT CARRIES IT IS AN INVERSION CONTROL -- feed two inputs that must produce OPPOSITE verdicts, and if they agree the seam is inert. SCOPE, owner correction the same day: the MARKET-SIMULATION half of this is WkAutoQuant-only -- that repo has replay tooling and live price fixtures and most repos have neither, so do not read this as a demand for a simulator. WHAT TRANSFERS EVERYWHERE is the cheap half and it needs no simulation at all: open the wired proto, lift the changed line by index, compile it, evaluate it against hand-built fixtures with the surrounding names stubbed, and require an inversion control. That works on a guard, a hook, a config resolver, anything. WHERE THE FULL TWO-LAYER FORM WITH REPLAY LIVES: the WkAutoQuant project CLAUDE.md, section 0-A. WHY, measured the day the owner approved it: the per-code exit cost seam passed diff, wc -l, AST name-set and a delegate's independent six-item gate, and NONE of those four executes anything. Layer one returned 8/8 and proved instrument_cost and harvest_anchor behave, which is a fact about MODULES. Layer two lifted host lines 892 and 932 out of the proto and evaluated them: SVIX skipped and AMD passed at the SAME PnL of 0.90 percent, SVIX straddles_both_below_cost and AMD straddles_breakeven_fires. That separation is the only thing that proved the promoted TEXT consumes the value. A delegate's own suite could not even run from ROOT's seat, because the module it imports does not exist in the local tree at all -- which is precisely the defect being fixed, the host never importing it, so the staging walk could not see it either. A DEFECT THAT HIDES ITS OWN VERIFICATION IS THE NORMAL CASE HERE, not the exception. AND THE RULE THAT PRECEDES ALL OF IT: when you build a wkedit --old-file from a sed LINE RANGE, verify the result by its BRACES and never by the diff -- an off-by-one there silently produces uncompilable source that diff review cannot catch, because the diff is computed from the same wrong range that caused the defect. Measured 2026-09-02 on WebCommands.Part1.cs: a range beginning one line early swallowed the blank line before GetSessionTag and left the method's own closing brace behind, so an orphaned brace landed right after the replacement comment; wkedit reported one clean replacement and printed a diff showing exactly the intended removal, nothing in its output was wrong, and the file no longer compiled. After any such extraction, read across the seam and count that the previous member's closing brace and the next member's opening each appear exactly once. AND THE RULE THIS SITS BESIDE: every piece of coding work is THREE artifacts and nothing less -- AND ALL THREE CAN BE PRESENT WHILE THE PROTO STILL CANNOT COMPILE, measured 2026-08-27, so add a host-declaration check ahead of them. A delegated proto for the missing [LOG] emit returned a correct body (Console.Error.WriteLine of the exact six-character prefix, stderr not stdout, gated on the file having opened, wrapped in try/catch) plus a self-test asserting the prefix and the Substring round-trip. Every stated constraint satisfied, three artifacts delivered. AND IT CANNOT COMPILE: the proto declares public sealed PARTIAL class TeeTextWriter while canonical TeeTextWriter.cs line 17 declares public sealed class TeeTextWriter : TextWriter with no partial keyword, and C# requires that keyword on EVERY declaration of a partial type, so wiring it as delivered breaks the build. THE REPORT SAID dotnet run EXIT 0 -- true and irrelevant, because that was a separate test project and never the CLI project containing the proto, so the proto had never been compiled by anything. WORSE, the self-test never called the proto either: it rebuilt the emitted string inline, so deleting the proto file entirely would still have left it passing 3 of 3. TWO RULES THIS ADDS. First, grep the canonical host for its type declaration and compare keyword-for-keyword BEFORE reviewing any logic -- it costs one grep and reviewing logic inside a file that cannot compile is wasted review. Second, a brief asking for a partial-class extract must ALSO name the one-word host edit that makes it legal, because a proto file alone cannot open a closed type and a delegate will not add what the brief did not ask for. The host edit is safe in isolation -- adding partial changes nothing for any caller and needs no caller audit -- it only needs to clear whatever lock guards the host, which for a 400-plus line file is this very procedure again. Original rule follows: when you build a wkedit --old-file from a sed LINE RANGE, verify the result by its BRACES and never by the diff -- an off-by-one there silently produces uncompilable source that diff review cannot catch, because the diff is computed from the same wrong range that caused the defect. Measured 2026-09-02 on WebCommands.Part1.cs: a range beginning one line early swallowed the blank line before GetSessionTag and left the method's own closing brace behind, so an orphaned brace landed right after the replacement comment; wkedit reported one clean replacement and printed a diff showing exactly the intended removal, nothing in its output was wrong, and the file no longer compiled. After any such extraction, read across the seam and count that the previous member's closing brace and the next member's opening each appear exactly once. AND THE RULE THIS SITS BESIDE: every piece of coding work is THREE artifacts and nothing less -- an EXTRACTION proto, a WIRING (wired) proto, and a SELF-TEST. Owner directive 2026-08-25, stated in those words and marked ABSOLUTE, never to be violated. WHEN: any turn where source is about to be written, by you or by a delegate, however small the change looks -- a one-line seam counts. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wksplit-cs-utility-howto for the extract-first mechanics, then write the brief demanding all three BY NAME, and refuse the return as incomplete when fewer than three arrive. WHY: measured the day the owner gave the rule -- one round returned a 40-line file labelled WIRED PROTO against a 422-line canonical, and the very next round returned none at all while reporting success and offering a menu of options instead. The rule caught both; without it each would have shipped as done. The cheapest detector is one number: a wired proto is a byte copy plus a seam, so its line count must sit within a couple of lines of canonical, and checking that exposes a fake before any diff is read. FOURTH ARTIFACT, demanded later by the resolve guard: an EVIDENCE SCRIPT under .wkappbot/evidence/ that re-proves the fix from a clean shell, written while the fix is fresh. Shape that passed 13/13: ev-2026-08-25-divider-matcher.sh. A happy-path-only script is not evidence -- the REFUSALS prove the change is narrow. This is the FIRST step of this skill because it is the first thing a session must do, not the seventeenth; it sat at step 8 until the owner found it buried there and ordered it to the top. Treat a delegation that returns fewer than three artifacts as incomplete and redispatch per the loop step, never as something ROOT patches by hand. Unconditionally delegate THREE things to a cheap tier (Haiku by default, per claude-code-agent-tier-routing step 7) in one brief -- (1) EXTRACT-FIRST: lift the target logic into its own small module BEFORE editing, per wksplit-cs-utility steps 21/23, so canonical only ever gains a Test-Path + dot-source + one call (step 6 of this skill); (2) the WIRED PROTO: a byte-copy of canonical with only that seam added, never a hand-summarized rewrite (step 8); (3) a SELF-TEST naming every case, with at least two NEGATIVE cases proving the guarded behaviour still refuses (proto-to-live-wiring-howto step 8). The brief must carry the four layers from -howto step 6 (exact steps, anti-confabulation raw-paste, prove-the-artifact exit with a BYTES/LINES/PARSE_ERRORS line before any PASS, narrow guardrails naming what NOT to touch) and the file-naming discipline from -howto steps 13-15 (stage via a .txt with no p-r-o substring for a new locked file; name only files the agent will read/create, never an incidental filename in prose). ROOT then does the diff-verify + git-mv landing itself (this skill's own promotion sequence, step 10 of -howto) -- delegation builds the proto, ROOT alone lands it. //why:The core principle: execute the seam to verify it works, never inspect code alone //why:Seams must be tested through execution, not code inspection //why:verify wkroot agy command path by running it live, not by reading wkroot source-opus //why:verify wkroot agy command path by running it live, not by reading wkroot source-opus //why:Seams must be tested through execution, not code inspection-haiku

DECISION, AND IT COMES BEFORE EVERYTHING ELSE IN THIS SKILL: TODO: build .tmp/Get-WkLetterEditIsFirstAttempt-proto.ps1 (session-JSONL-based first-edit-attempt check in wkappbot-kih, same pattern as Get-WkLastDelegationTs in wkharness-guards-busyfleet.ps1) and .tmp/Invoke-WkLetterEditGate-wired-proto.ps1 (byte-copy with RootDir derived from FilePath via git rev-parse, same pattern as Get-WkLetterRepoRoot) via the txt-scratch-then-wkappbot-file-write promotion method. Verification: both protos must actually run and print real self-test output, not just parse-check. ORIGINAL STEP FOLLOWS. DECISION: BUILD THE MODULE -- THE EXTRACTION PROTO -- FIRST. It OUTRANKS the wired proto (owner ruling 2026-08-25). CONFIRMED 2026-09-08 on --move-to: committed the module (SkillCommand.Edit.MoveStep.cs) and its StepOps wiring FIRST, leaving the wired proto (SkillCommand.Edit.cs's flag-parsing seam) stashed and inert until its own line-growth fold lands separately -- the module survives and is reviewable even while the seam is still being shaped. AND THAT RULE HAS A FAILURE MODE ITS OWN AUTHOR WALKED INTO THE SAME DAY, so read the guard before the rule: CHECKING WHETHER AN EXTRACTION EXISTS IS NOT PERMISSION TO SKIP ONE. The test is whether a module already owns THE EXACT CONCERN THIS CHANGE TOUCHES -- not whether some neighbouring module exists, and not whether a value the seam happens to call is importable. Measured 2026-08-25: ROOT found instrument_cost already promoted and unwired, correctly told the exit delegate to reuse it, then carried the same sentence into the ENTRY brief where it was FALSE -- the US entry-discount arithmetic was inline in a 418-line file and had never been extracted at all. Three rounds were dispatched to add a call INTO that file, and every one was uncommittable by construction, because fat-source-growth refuses any commit that lengthens a file past the 400-line cap. THE EXTRACTION WAS THE PROMOTION PATH, not paperwork: moving the concern out SHRINKS the host and is the only thing that makes the fix landable, which wksplit-cs-utility step 5 already states. ROOT reported the wall as a blocker instead of recognising the door. AND THE GUARD CANNOT SAVE YOU: agent-brief-guard checks three skill reads and the five-part SPEC and nothing else, so a brief that says add the call passes cleanly with the extraction silently skipped. Put EXTRACT FIRST in the Goal line yourself. NOW THE ORIGINAL RULE: BEFORE YOU BUILD ONE, CHECK WHETHER THE EXTRACTION ALREADY EXISTS AND IS MERELY UNWIRED -- in a mature repo that is the COMMON case, and reading extraction-first literally then produces a duplicate, which is the bandaid this repo forbids by name. The tell costs one command: run wk-unwired.cmd, or grep the running host for the module name and count the call sites; a promoted module with ZERO callers is a FINISHED extraction waiting for a seam, so the brief must tell the delegate to PROVE it and wire it, and must say outright that writing a second resolver is an automatic reject. Measured 2026-08-25 on a live money defect: the US scalper compared every exit against ONE flat cost constant while holding SVIX, a PTP whose true round-trip cost is 11.32 percent against that flat 0.21, so a 10.4 percent loss read as a profit worth banking -- and TWO finished extractions were already sitting unwired, instrument_cost.round_trip_cost_pct which is pure and self-tested, and harvest_trigger_proto whose earnsave_decision and clock_harvest_decision both already take a parameter their own docstrings call per-code round-trip cost. Grepping the production host for instrument_cost and ptp_cost returned zero. The defect was never a missing calculation, it was a missing call: the module is the asset that survives, the wired proto is disposable scaffolding that exists only to make the seam reviewable, and the self-test belongs to the module rather than to the seam. A change small enough to inline is exactly the change that must NOT be inlined -- an inline compound condition passes every gate at net-zero growth and permanently costs you the ability to test, reuse or simulate that decision. Promote the module UNWIRED rather than hoarding it in .tmp, which gets swept. The full rule and the dated failure that earned it are in the step beginning THE MODULE (EXTRACTION) PROTO IS ARTIFACT NUMBER ONE. ONLY THEN does the rest of this skill apply -- starting with: verify by DIFF before you verify by test, because a passing self-test says nothing about where the code was inserted. WHEN: any proto comes back green. HOW: run git diff --no-index tools/<file> .tmp/<file>-proto and read the CONTEXT lines around every hunk, then re-run the self-test yourself -- see wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for why a report is not evidence. MEASURED 2026-09-19, THE EXACT MECHANISM THAT DEFEATS A ROOT MERGE PAST OMEGA, because the old wording said dispatch a sector without saying how you know you must. ROOT copied a verified wired proto over a harness file and git diff --stat printed 1 insertion; the VERY NEXT command found no change at all, and a grep for the new symbol returned 0. So the PostToolUse rollback reverts a ROOT harness write INSIDE THE SAME CALL, which means the standing advice to commit in the next call cannot save it -- there is no next call early enough. THE DISCRIMINATOR, and run it before concluding anything: copy, then IMMEDIATELY grep the target for a symbol only the new line contains. A count of 1 means the write held; a 0 means the rollback reached it and the merge must be delegated. A sector's write to the SAME folder persisted in the same session, which is what makes the delegation the remedy rather than a workaround. AND THE PART THAT IS STILL ROOT'S, so this is not read as permission to hand the whole thing over: ROOT builds the wired proto, ROOT re-runs the self-test, ROOT fires the module at the REAL tree, and ROOT re-verifies the landed diff and commits it. Only the byte copy moves. THE MERGE INTO CANONICAL IS ROOT S AT EVERY TRANSCRIPT SIZE, INCLUDING PAST OMEGA. The merge stays ROOT's at every transcript size, because the control that makes delegation safe is the byte diff, and a sector able to write canonical can also edit the .tmp proto, which makes the diff come back clean over content ROOT never approved -- and for a BRAND NEW file there is no canonical to diff against at all, so the diff proves copying and never fidelity. WHAT IS TRUE in the old text: the omega guard does refuse ROOT file creation and it wins mechanically, measured at 13.3 MB where the file-write command, a plain cp and git mv with force were all refused by name. WHAT FOLLOWS FROM IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT WAS WRITTEN: when ROOT cannot merge, the work does NOT stop -- dispatch a sector for the identical write (a sector is empirically exempt from the ROOT-only omega block, confirmed live 2026-09-13), pay whatever gate refuses the sector and redispatch with a corrected brief, and repeat until either it lands or every route is genuinely exhausted. A hard stop must never be written as a licence: that shape reads as permission exactly when a session is out of options and least able to argue, which is exactly why record the blocker was struck from step 3 of this same skill 2026-09-13 -- if every route is truly exhausted, the honest report is an OPEN BLOCKER for the owner, never a quiet stopping point. WHEN: a verified proto is ready late in a long session and you are deciding who merges it into canonical. HOW: run wkappbot skill read foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore for the rule that wiring is ROOT's charge, then TRY IT YOURSELF FIRST and let the refusal decide -- a plain cp of the proto onto its canonical path either works, in which case ROOT wires it, or returns the omega refusal naming the transcript size, in which case dispatch the promotion with the byte-identical-copy contract and verify the result from the canonical path yourself. Do not assume either rule applies without the one command that settles it. WHY: measured 2026-09-05 in personal-docs, both directions in the same session. Earlier, at under 5 MB, cp of launcher_rc_selftest.py from .tmp into tools/ succeeded and ROOT wired it directly. Later, at 5.3 MB, the identical command on portal_login_check.py was refused with the message that creating a NEW file outside .tmp is delegated at this scale and should be handed to a sector or dispatched via Agent.cmd. DECISION: 🔴 CORRECTED 2026-09-11 BY OWNER DIRECTIVE, and the old wording is the root that taught sessions to abandon work: it said a blocked promotion should be LEFT UNCOMMITTED in the working tree. NEVER LEAVE VERIFIED-OR-UNVERIFIED SOURCE UNCOMMITTED. His words: an expensive source change is a HUNDRED TIMES more important than the letter, so COMMIT IT. A working tree is the one place work is silently lost -- a branch switch, a stash, a cleanup sweep or the next session's checkout all discard it, and the gates that blocked the push do NOT block a local commit. THE ORDER IS: commit locally FIRST, saying in the message exactly what is unverified and why, then fight the promotion gate. A commit is free, reversible and recoverable; an uncommitted tree is none of those. TWO SEPARATE HARD-ABORT DESIGNS COLLIDE ON A CROSS-BRANCH LETTER MERGE, measured 2026-09-12: wk-gitsync's mergepush NEVER lets HANDOFF.md resolve via keep-ours even when explicitly named (by design, to protect the letter), so a genuinely diverged letter aborts the WHOLE merge regardless of what else is listed. Editing wk-gitsync.ps1 to add an opt-in escape hits a SEPARATE wall at omega tier: a study-locked source edit is delegation-only, and the delegate brief then hits brief-quote-gate refusing to count a skill-read as genuine even when a real 40-plus-char verbatim quote from that skill IS present -- three redispatch attempts all reported quotes none of them. WHEN this combination recurs, switch strategy rather than reformatting the same brief: complete the merge FIRST with HANDOFF.md kept on the CURRENT branch's own content, then attempt the letter content-replacement as ONE separate follow-up commit once the merge has made the other branch's commits real ancestors of HEAD. CROSS-BRANCH HANDOFF.md GATE ORDERING, measured 2026-09-12: handoff-manifest-gate reads COMMITTED ancestor history, so a letter carried over from another branch (a merge, a cherry-pick, a manual git checkout <ref> -- HANDOFF.md) is refused on the TARGET branch until that branch's own history contains the commits the manifest cites -- which for a plain merge only becomes true AFTER the merge lands, making the gate unsatisfiable if you try to land the letter content inside the merge commit itself. Sequence that actually works: commit the adopted HANDOFF.md ALONE on the target branch FIRST (a plain content copy, no merge involved yet), let that fail if it must, then do the real merge/graph-joining operation afterward once the ancestry problem is no longer in the way for that specific file. AND THE RING TO RECOGNISE, measured the same day: the letter gate refuses to write HANDOFF.md while tracked source is uncommitted, while the manifest and wish gates refuse the COMMIT until the letter carries a row -- the exit is git stash push with a pathspec, which parks the source, opens the letter, and is undone with git checkout stash@{0} -- pathspec. What must never be forced through is a risky offsetting DELETION under time pressure. PYTHON FORM OF THE EXTRACT-FIRST SEAM, added 2026-08-06 on the owner's instruction after I skipped extraction on a 2,932-line trading source. Steps 3 and 23 already require it, but both are written in PowerShell terms -- a Test-Path, a dot-source, one call -- so a reader working in Python has no obvious mapping and may conclude the rule does not apply. IT APPLIES. The trigger in step 6 is the 400-line cap and is language-neutral; a 2,932-line Python module is nine times past it. THE PYTHON SEAM is the direct analogue: a module-level import of the new module, and ONE call at the site where the logic used to sit. There is no Test-Path equivalent because a missing import fails loudly at load rather than silently at call, which is the correct failure direction anyway. Keep the import at module scope, never inside the function, for the same reason step 8 gives for dot-sources. PRECEDENT ALREADY IN THIS REPO, which is what makes it concrete rather than aspirational: scripts/scalper_breakout_sell.py is exactly such an extraction -- the percentage-breakout exit was lifted out of the fat scalper into its own module, and the host now imports it and calls one function. Any new extraction should match that shape rather than inventing another. WHAT I DID WRONG, so the next reader recognises it: the change was three lines, so I briefed an in-place edit of those three lines and never asked whether the surrounding block belonged in a module. Size of the change is NOT the test; size of the HOST is. A one-line edit to a 2,900-line file still costs the next editor a full study-lock read of that file, which is precisely the cost extraction exists to stop paying. THE RULE RESTATED FOR ANY LANGUAGE, AND IT IS UNCONDITIONAL: the delegated deliverable is ALWAYS a new module plus a host that gains only an import and a call, never an in-place edit however small. There is NO size condition on either side. Owner directive 2026-08-07, given precisely because the conditional wording caused confusion and a wrong-shaped brief: do not ask whether the host is over the cap, do not ask whether the change is small, do not weigh whether extraction is worth it. Extract first, every time. The prior wording made this a judgement call and a judgement call is what gets skipped under time pressure. //why:using the proto-to-live approach for this promotion-haiku //why:using the proto-to-live approach for this promotion-haiku //why:extract-first seam python analogue
